learningObjectives: Distinguish TestCase-Design coverage planning from Test Data Service item management.
Identify suitable data and explicitly track its state as tests change it.
Explain the scope of Find locking and non-locking ReadOnly access.
Plan independent practice without assuming single-use data or automatic application synchronization.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Test Data Service in a test-data workflow

elements.description: A test-data workflow must provide usable inputs, keep necessary state and define how data is reused or retired. This lesson concentrates on Test Data Service, not a verified catalog of Tricentis product offerings.

elements.title: Test Data Service responsibilities
items: Store items grouped by type in a repository.
Find suitable items and explicitly create, update, move or delete them.
Use the web data view, Standard Modules or the installed API definition according to the task.

elements.text: This is an independent Tosca 2026.1 documentation-based introduction. The Academy video version and its historical product comparisons have not been verified.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: TestCase Design vs. Test Data Service

elements.description: TestCase-Design models test combinations and concrete values through TestSheets, Attributes and Instances. It helps plan coverage and instantiate TestCase templates; it does not make an application input inherently safe for simultaneous use.

elements.term: Item management with Test Data Service
elements.description: TDS stores items that tests can select and change. Reuse depends on the test scenario and current data state. Stored items are not inherently single-use: a read can be non-locking, and a selected item can be used again after its lock is released if the scenario permits.

A practice login may use a disposable username and a fake password. A payment workflow may need an already-created practice account. Decide which inputs are valid before running the application actions.

bulletPoints: Coverage combinations and runtime item state answer different questions.
Neither tool guarantees that shared application data is safe to change concurrently.

elements.description: Prepare or import suitable practice data, then select an item matching the intended preconditions. A create operation stores an item; it is not a guarantee of automatic production-data masking or valid account provisioning in the application.

Verify the application result, then explicitly store any new identifier or state required by later tests. A property called Status is not automatically updated merely because an application action or TestCase completed.

Suppose two tests both change a practice account. Separate accounts may permit parallel execution; if one shared account is required, coordinate access and verify its current state. Do not turn this example into a rule that all account tests must run sequentially.

Find & provide item locks the selected item. Expert ReadOnly retrieves data without acquiring a lock; it does not unlock an existing one. Find releases its lock at execution completion, on failure or a new loop iteration. Locking test-data access does not automatically protect every application-side operation.

bulletPoints: Acquiring suitable data and maintaining its current state are separate tasks.
Use explicit selection, updates and an intentional reuse policy.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming TDS items are always single-use
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating storage in TDS as proof that data can never be read again or used without a lock.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the operation and scenario: ReadOnly does not acquire a lock, and reuse can be allowed after a lock is released.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming application state is mirrored automatically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a Status property, account identifier or consumed flag to update without a configured operation.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify the application outcome and explicitly update the required item properties.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly distinguishes TestCase-Design from Test Data Service?

options.text: TestCase Design data is dynamic and consumable; TDS data is static and reusable.
TestCase-Design plans combinations and values; TDS manages stored items whose selection, state and reuse depend on configured operations.
There is no meaningful difference between the two.
TDS data can only be used by non-UI TestCases.

practiceQuiz.hint: Coverage planning is different from managing stored item state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TestCase-Design models combinations and concrete values. TDS manages test items; neither distinction implies that data is always static, inherently single-use or automatically safe for simultaneous application changes.

optionExplanations.A: This reverses the tool responsibilities and incorrectly assigns inherent static or consumable behavior.
optionExplanations.B: TestCase-Design plans combinations while TDS manages stored items through configured operations.
optionExplanations.C: Coverage planning and stored item management have distinct responsibilities.
optionExplanations.D: TDS data can feed UI tests too; the documented Find example inserts retrieved values into an application.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TDS operation retrieves an item without acquiring a lock?
practiceQuiz.hint: Reading without acquiring a lock is different from releasing a lock.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Expert ReadOnly reads without acquiring a lock. It does not mean that an existing lock is released or that all application-side access is coordinated.

optionExplanations.A: Find acquires a lock on the selected item, so it is not the non-locking read operation.
optionExplanations.B: ReadOnly retrieves data without acquiring a lock; unlocking an existing item is a different operation.
optionExplanations.C: DeleteAll is a destructive deletion operation, not a way to read an item.
optionExplanations.D: Moving an item changes its type membership, not a non-locking read.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which pair of concerns does the independent test-data workflow in this lesson address?

options.text: Writing TestCases and executing them on time.
Acquiring specific test data, and ensuring the state of that data is efficiently tracked.
Installing Tosca Server and configuring the network.

practiceQuiz.hint: One concern is suitable inputs; the other is their state after use.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Prepare or find suitable data and explicitly maintain the state that later tests require. Neither task is automatically solved by storing an item in TDS.

optionExplanations.A: Writing and scheduling tests are broader activities; they do not identify the two data concerns.
optionExplanations.B: Suitable input acquisition and explicit state tracking are the two concerns illustrated here.
optionExplanations.C: Installation and network configuration are prerequisites, not this pair of data-management concerns.
optionExplanations.D: Attributes and Instances support design modeling but do not describe maintaining runtime data state.

quickRecap.value: This independent introduction covers Test Data Service item management.
Model combinations and concrete values for coverage and template instantiation.
Store, select and explicitly change test data; reuse depends on the scenario.
Find suitable data for the intended preconditions.
Store verified identifiers and state changes explicitly.
Find acquires a lock; ReadOnly does not acquire one or release an existing lock.
Find releases locks after execution, on failure or at a new loop iteration.
